jane (acct:AcmeCorp): Hey team — weird one. After we shifted ~40% traffic to a Dedicated pool yesterday, the embeddings for identical inputs diverged. cosine(hosted, dedicated) ~0.66 for a single short prompt where it used to be >0.99. No obvious truncation. Request IDs: hosted=rq_ht_01, dedicated=rq_dt_02. Can we triage?

anna (Support): Sorry, that sounds bad. Can you paste a tiny reproducible payload and the model + variant you called? Also any headers like X-Redwood-Batch or batch_window_ms you set?

jane (acct:AcmeCorp): Minimal payload below. We call model `redwood-embed-lite-v1` with no explicit variant. No special headers set.

jane (acct:AcmeCorp): ```json
{"input":"Kubernetes rollout health check","model":"redwood-embed-lite-v1","top_k":0}
```

liam (ML Eng): Thanks. Quick Q: are you using Hosted embedding endpoint vs Dedicated endpoint URLs? Did you pin model versions? Dedicated recently got a canary with q4_0 quantized variants for cost savings.

jane (acct:AcmeCorp): We pointed 60% -> hosted api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings and 40% -> dedicated.dRedwood/acme/v1/embeddings. We didn't pin explicitly.

noah (Infra SRE): Noted. We had an autoscaler tweak yesterday: batch_window_ms default increased from 10 -> 25ms in Dedicated to reduce API pressure. That can change batching behavior.

liam (ML Eng): Batching shouldn't change vector dimensionality, but quantized variant can change low-level numeric representation and give small drift. Drift that large (0.66) suggests model variant mismatch (full precision vs quantized) or a different pooling/padding path being hit.

anna (Support): Can you run a quick compare? Two calls back-to-back one to hosted and one to dedicated with explicit headers: `X-Redwood-Model-Variant: full_precision` and `X-Redwood-Batching: false`.

jane (acct:AcmeCorp): Running now. Output: hosted vec length=1536, dedicated vec length=1536. Cosine = 0.67. So dims match but values diverge.

liam (ML Eng): Ok dims equal — rules out shape bug. Next: confirm batching/padding path. Try forcing batch_window_ms=0 via header to disable batching (or set batching: false in body) and force variant: `model_variant=full_fp32` in body if supported. Re-run 10 times sequentially.

jane (acct:AcmeCorp): Ran sequential with `batch_window_ms:0` and `model_variant:full_fp32` — now cosine ~0.995.

noah (Infra SRE): That nails it — the Dedicated default batching config + quantized variant together produced a different execution path. In small prompts, the quantized fast-path plus 25ms window caused request coalescing and a different KV cache/prefix pad heuristic. When you forced no-batching + full_fp32 it used the same inference kernel as hosted.

liam (ML Eng): Root cause summary: Dedicated pool had two config diffs from Hosted: (1) default `model_variant` fallback to `q4_0` for cost, (2) `batch_window_ms` increased to 25ms. Interaction caused different tokenization/padding order in the batched execution leading to lower similarity for short inputs.

anna (Support): Short-term fix: on your Dedicated config set explicit `model_variant=full_fp32` or call with header `X-Redwood-Batching: false`. We'll also push a patch so Dedicated respects model_variant parity by default for rolling pools serving live traffic.

jane (acct:AcmeCorp): That works for us as a workaround. Any perf/cost impact we should expect?

liam (ML Eng): full_fp32 will increase token cost ~1.8x on Dedicated for that model. If you need cost parity consider `q4_0` with `batch_window_ms=10` (lower window) — that makes the batching behavior closer to Hosted while keeping quant savings. We'll do throughput tests.

noah (Infra SRE): Action items: 1) revert Dedicated canary to previous batching default for affected pools OR 2) add a flag to surface batching defaults per-customer in control plane; 3) run a canary aligning batch_window_ms between Hosted and Dedicated. I'll open a deploy ticket.

deploy-bot: Deploy ticket opened: DP-5943 — align-dedicated-batching-defaults (assigned to infra, priority P2).

anna (Support): I'm updating the customer with repro steps and toggles. Will confirm when infra has a canary.

liam (ML Eng): For reproducibility here's a curl to compare: ```bash
# hosted
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"Kubernetes rollout health check","model":"redwood-embed-lite-v1","model_variant":"full_fp32","batching":false}'

# dedicated
curl -s -X POST https://dedicated.acme.redwood/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DED_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"Kubernetes rollout health check","model":"redwood-embed-lite-v1","model_variant":"full_fp32","batching":false}'
```

jane (acct:AcmeCorp): Thanks — running these as smoke tests in our CI. We'll report if any regression.

anna (Support): FYI billing-bot picked up the dedicated pool change yesterday. billing-bot, can you confirm no surprise billing spike?

billing-bot: No immediate spike flagged; Dedicated quantized usage is lower per-token, but switching to full_fp32 will show higher usage cost metric. Notified AcmeCorp billing contact.

noah (Infra SRE): Can we also add a short regression test in CI that runs embedding parity checks for a handful of sample prompts when a batcher change is rolled? Would catch this earlier.

liam (ML Eng): Agreed. I'll add a test: run N pairs of hosted vs dedicated with batching toggles and assert cosine >= 0.98 for canonical prompts. If fail, block rollout.

anna (Support): Great. I'll keep the thread open until DP-5943 canary is complete and AcmeCorp confirms. :eyes:

jane (acct:AcmeCorp): Appreciated — will close when CI smoke passes. :thumbsup:
